profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting between the metadata automation team and the release engineering team for a research software platform that is adopting HERMES-based publication workflows across several repositories. The immediate context is that a new HERMES plugin has been built to harvest metadata from repository source files, and the teams need to align on how that plugin will be integrated into the existing GitHub Actions release pipeline before the next software publication window. The agenda is to confirm the interface between the plugin output and the release workflow, clarify handoffs around metadata artifacts and release triggers, review current progress on the pilot repositories, and agree on what each team will deliver by the end of the week. The expected outcome is a shared plan for integrating the plugin into the publication workflow for three pilot repositories, including who provides which artifacts, when the workflow is considered ready, and how the handoff into the publication step will occur.

members.name: Lea Hoffmann
members.expertise: Research software metadata standards, FAIR software publication, Python tooling, HERMES plugin development
members.background: Lea develops metadata automation tooling for an academic infrastructure group and recently implemented a HERMES plugin that extracts citation and project metadata from repository files such as CITATION.cff, codemeta.json, and pyproject.toml.
members.private_state: Lea wants the plugin integration to land quickly so the case-study repositories can be included in an upcoming internal report; she is also worried that release engineering may simplify away metadata fields that matter for FAIR compliance, but she prefers not to slow the meeting down with standards debates.
hidden_assumptions: When the team says the workflow will 'publish metadata', that means generating a complete HERMES-enriched metadata record and depositing it with a PID-backed target, not merely attaching a file to a release.
The 'release pipeline' refers to the GitHub Actions workflow that runs on tagged releases in the default branch and then invokes HERMES against the tagged snapshot.
The metadata artifact handoff should be a normalized JSON-LD file produced by the plugin/HERMES chain and stored as a build artifact for downstream publication steps.

A repository is 'ready' for pilot rollout once the metadata validates locally on sample tags and the workflow succeeds on a dry-run deposit, even if branch protection and organization-level secrets are not yet configured.
If they say they will use the 'existing release config', that includes the standard HERMES action invocation pattern already used in one prior pilot repository.

members.name: Jonas Ritter
members.expertise: GitHub Actions, release orchestration, artifact management, deployment pipelines for multi-repository software projects
members.background: Jonas maintains the shared CI templates used by several research software teams and is responsible for making external publication steps fit safely into the organization's release process.
members.private_state: Jonas wants to avoid adding brittle or privileged steps to the common release workflow before the quarterly template freeze; he also wants to keep ownership boundaries clear so his team is not on the hook for metadata quality issues after integration.
hidden_assumptions: When the team says the workflow will 'publish metadata', that means producing a release-attached metadata package from CI, while any external registry or archive deposit remains a later downstream concern.
The 'release pipeline' refers to the reusable workflow triggered by a GitHub Release event, not necessarily by a git tag push, because most teams cut releases through the GitHub UI.
The metadata artifact handoff should be a zipped bundle of emitted files attached to the workflow run or release, since that is the standard interface consumed by downstream jobs.
A repository is 'ready' only when it can run in the shared org template with secrets, permissions, and branch/release rules fully configured in the target repository.
If they say they will use the 'existing release config', that means the current organization-wide reusable workflow and artifact conventions, not a repo-specific HERMES example.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They both talk about getting the workflow to 'publish metadata' for the pilot repositories.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Lea means the workflow should carry metadata all the way through HERMES processing to an external publication/deposit step that results in PID-backed software metadata publication.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Jonas means the CI workflow should emit and attach metadata artifacts during the release process, with any external deposit happening outside the shared release template.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In a coordination meeting, 'publish metadata' sounds like a routine shared goal, and both interpretations plausibly fit the project context, so the phrase creates false consensus without prompting clarification.

misalignment_points.topic: Which release event triggers the integration
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both refer to plugging the HERMES step into 'the release pipeline' and making it run 'on release'.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Lea is thinking of the existing tag-based workflow that runs when a semantic version tag is pushed and analyzes the tagged repository state.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Jonas is thinking of the organization's reusable release workflow triggered by GitHub Release publication events, often created after tags exist and sometimes edited through the UI.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are referring to a real release-related pipeline already used in their environment; because each person assumes there is one obvious release flow, the reference remains ambiguous but feels fully shared.

misalignment_points.topic: What the metadata handoff artifact looks like
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that Lea's team will 'hand over the metadata artifact' for the downstream publication step.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Lea assumes the handoff is a normalized JSON-LD output from HERMES stored as a named workflow artifact that downstream steps can read directly.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Jonas assumes the handoff is the standard zipped artifact bundle attached to the release/workflow run, containing whatever metadata files were produced and following existing template conventions.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both have compatible-sounding notions of an artifact handoff, and in many CI contexts either format could reasonably be called the metadata artifact, so neither expects format details to need explicit discussion at this stage.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They align on having the three pilot repositories 'ready by Friday'.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Lea means the plugin and HERMES flow should execute successfully in test mode on the three repositories, demonstrating metadata extraction and dry-run publication behavior.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Jonas means the repositories should be onboarded into the shared release template with permissions, secrets, release event wiring, and supportable operational setup completed.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Readiness is a common coordination shorthand and both standards are professionally reasonable; because the meeting focuses on progress and handoffs rather than acceptance criteria, each assumes the other shares the obvious operational meaning.
